choices.why: The speaker labels in the print mark who asks about eating the divinity or the humanity (Nestorius) and who answers (Cyril).
ἴδε is the imperative 'see'; οὖν draws the conclusion.

choices.english: because of the Father who sent me
choices.why: διά with the accusative gives the cause.
rejected: through the Father who sent me

choices.why: The two abstract nouns Nestorius sets against each other.

pass_a_gloss: [CYRIL, continuing Hebrews 9:28 from the previous section] once having been brought forward (προσενεχθείς) for the carrying up of the sins of many, out of a second [time] without sin will be seen. And again: Sin he did not do, and deceit was not present in the mouth of him; and look, he himself brings himself forward on behalf of us; see (ἴδε) therefore, not on behalf of himself did he carry himself up, but on behalf of the people. [NESTORIUS] Of him saying: The one chewing (τρώγων) of me the flesh, and drinking of me the blood, will live through me, according as I live on account of (διὰ τόν) the one having sent me, Father. Whom then are you eating, heretic? The divinity (θεότητα), or the humanity (ἀνθρωπότητα)? For not did the Christ say, The one chewing of me the divinity, but, The flesh. [CYRIL] I on my part by faith partake (μεταλαμβάνω) of the of the life-making Word life-making flesh; whence the Savior declared: The ones eating out of this bread by no means will taste of death into the age; the ones [the text breaks off]
pass_b_english: '…having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, apart from sin' (Hebrews 9:28). And again: 'He committed no sin, and there was no deceit in his mouth' (1 Peter 2:22). And look, he himself offers himself for us. See, then: he did not offer himself up for himself, but for the people.

Nestorius says: Since he says, 'Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood will live through me, just as I live because of the Father who sent me' (John 6:56-57), what then do you eat, heretic? The divinity, or the humanity? For Christ did not say, 'Whoever eats my divinity,' but 'the flesh.'

απαξ προσενεχθεὶς εἰς τὸ πολλῶν ἀνενεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας, ἐκ δευτέρου χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας
ὀφθήσεται. Καὶ πάλιν· ̔Αμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν, καὶ δόλος οὐχ ὑπῆρχεν ἐν τῷ στόματι
αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἰδοὺ αὐτὸς ἑαυτὸν προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν· ιδε ουν οὐχ ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ
ἀνήνεγκεν αὑτὸν, ἀλλ' ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ. {ΝΕΣΤ.} Αὐτοῦ λέγοντος· ̔Ο τρώγων μου τὴν
σάρκα, καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αιμα, ζήσεται δι' ἐμοῦ, καθὼς ἐγὼ ζῶ διὰ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά
με Πατέρα. 76.253 Τίνα ουν ἐσθίεις, αἱρετικέ; τὴν θεότητα, η τὴν ἀνθρωπότητα; Οὐκ
ειπε γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς, ̔Ο τρώγων μου τὴν θεότητα, ἀλλὰ, Τὴν σάρκα. {ΚΥΡ.} ̓Εγὼ μὲν
πίστει μεταλαμβάνω τὴν τοῦ ζωοποιοῦ Λόγου ζωοποιοῦσαν σάρκα· οθεν ὁ Σωτὴρ
εφη· Οἱ ἐσθίοντες ἐκ τούτου τοῦ αρτου, οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· οἱ
